audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Aurora Levels 2-3, first item and two items, and called Level 1 a skill stage. That is close to the exact inverse of what the page's own whys say.
audit.why: Every why on the page describes an Akshan-sided lane from Level 2 to first item — "concede the step-up", "he hit-and-runs your single-target poke", "his swing-and-poke kite beats your tempo", "it deletes you", "your three-stack spirit sustain still can't out-DPS" — and gives Aurora only Level 1 and the two-item stage. The enum array contradicted its own explanation on six of seven rows. 47.67% over 86 games fits the Akshan-sided middle, not an Aurora-sided one.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Aurora / Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Aurora, matching the packet chart and the page's existing whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase named Aurora's ultimate "Between the Worlds" — no such ability — and framed 6 as her spike. Level 6 is Akshan's spike in this lane, and no ultimate cooldown or range was given anywhere.
audit.why: Comeuppance is 100/85/70 seconds at 2500 range and its damage is based on the target's missing health, so it converts Akshan's Avengerang chip (9/8/7/6/5, 850 range) into a screen-edge kill. Between Worlds is 140/120/100 — 40 seconds longer at rank 1 — so Aurora cannot answer it cast for cast.
audit.corrected: Comeuppance (100s, 2500 range) scales with your missing health — his Q chip is the setup, so heal up before stepping into his line.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction in this matchup is never stated: Comeuppance is a line projectile that stops on the first thing it hits, and Heroic Swing can be knocked off. The page treats the ultimate as unavoidable ("your W leap can't dodge a locked channel") and treats the swing as a free escape.
audit.why: Riot's text for Comeuppance: he "fires all stored bullets, dealing damage based on missing health to the first champion, minion, or structure hit." A minion in the line eats the whole thing — standing behind your own wave is the counterplay, not dodging. Heroic Swing (E, 18/16.5/15/13.5/12, 800): he "fires a grappling hook into terrain then swings around it... He can jump off early or gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain" — it needs terrain to anchor, so it is dead in open lane, and body-blocking ends it. Dirty Fighting (P) shields him on every third hit from attacks or abilities against a champion, so his first shield eats your burst window. Going Rogue (W, 18/14/10/6/2) camouflage decays fast when he is not in brush or near terrain, which is why he roams along walls.
audit.corrected: Comeuppance hits the first champion, minion or structure in its line — stand behind your own wave and it eats the execute instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[0].d described Heroic Swing as "his dash + camera swing escape" with no cooldown and no condition on it.
audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and needs terrain to hook into, and a champion collision knocks him off mid-swing. Both facts change whether you can punish him for using it.
audit.corrected: Heroic Swing (18s) needs terrain to hook, and colliding with a champion knocks him off mid-swing.

audit.why: The packet flagged "Use Going Rogue" (wants.foe[1]) and "Use Between Worlds" (late) as probable wrong ability names. Both are correct: Going Rogue is Akshan's W and Between Worlds is Aurora's R in Riot's kit files. These are suspectNames false positives and no name edit is warranted.

notes: The page's prose and its level chart disagreed on six of seven rows; the prose was right, so only the enum arrays were changed and no why needed rewriting. Same cross-cutting fabrication as elsewhere in this champion: 'mid' and 'late' claim Between Worlds turns Aurora untargetable, which is not in Riot's description of the ability — logged in unverified, not asserted in any new text.
